name: Cash Margin
description: A percentage of the facility amount held in a blocked account. The strongest security — instantly liquid. Common on LCs and LGs (e.g. 10–100% depending on client strength).

name: Real Estate Mortgage
description: A registered first-degree mortgage over property. Strong security but slow to realise; value should be supported by a recent independent valuation with a sensible margin (e.g. lend against 50–70%).

name: Share Pledge
description: Pledge over listed shares. Liquid but volatile — requires a margin cushion and top-up triggers if the price falls.

name: Assignment of Contract Proceeds
description: The project employer pays contract proceeds directly to the client's account with the bank. The natural security for contracting facilities — the repayment source itself is captured.

name: Assignment of Receivables
description: Specific invoices/receivables are assigned to the bank, with the debtor notified to pay the bank directly. Standard for discounting facilities.

name: Personal Guarantee
description: Guarantee from the owners/partners. More moral commitment than hard security — keeps owners on the hook but is only as good as their personal wealth.

name: Corporate Guarantee
description: Guarantee from a parent or sister company. Useful when the borrower is a thin subsidiary of a strong group — always check the guarantor's own financials and a board resolution authorising it.
